limits.units: °C-WBGT, 1-hour time-weighted average; M = metabolic rate in watts

metabolic_rates.source: Representative metabolic rate classes 0-4 of ISO 7243:2017 (65, 100, 165, 230, 290 W/m2) converted for a standard 1.8 m2 body surface area. Sites should replace these with task-specific estimates where available.

light.label: Light
light.examples: Sitting or standing with light manual work, driving, inspecting

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.examples: Sustained hand/arm work, walking 3.5-5.5 km/h, operating hand tools

heavy.label: Heavy
heavy.examples: Intense arm and trunk work, carrying heavy material, shovelling, sawing

very_heavy.label: Very heavy
very_heavy.examples: Very intense activity at fast to maximum pace, digging, climbing with loads

work_rest_regimes.source: Work/rest cycles per hour shown alongside the RAL/REL curves in NIOSH 2016. The 1-hour TWA metabolic rate is computed as (work_min * M_work + rest_min * M_rest) / 60, with rest assumed in the same thermal environment (conservative).

clothing_adjustment_factors.source: Clothing adjustment values (°C-WBGT added to measured WBGT) reproduced in NIOSH 2016 and the OSHA Technical Manual Sec. III Ch. 4, based on Bernard and co-workers. Values apply to the listed ensembles only.

long_sleeved_protective.label: Long-sleeved woven protective clothing
long_sleeved_protective.note: Treated as woven work clothing (long-sleeved shirt and trousers).

vapor_barrier_coveralls.label: Limited-use vapour-barrier coveralls
vapor_barrier_coveralls.note: Guidance cautions that WBGT-based assessment is of limited validity for vapour-barrier and encapsulating ensembles; physiological monitoring by qualified personnel is advised.

specialized_ppe.label: Specialized protective equipment (unspecified)
specialized_ppe.note: Thermal impact differs by ensemble. A site OHS professional must configure a documented adjustment value before an assessment can be produced.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.note: Unknown status is NOT treated as acclimatized; the more protective RAL is applied and confidence is reduced.

acclimatization.schedule_new_workers: NIOSH 2016: new workers should have no more than 20% of the usual duration of heat exposure on day 1 and no more than a 20% increase each additional day.
acclimatization.schedule_experienced_workers: NIOSH 2016: workers with previous experience should have no more than 50% on day 1, 60% on day 2, 80% on day 3 and 100% on day 4.

risk_categories.source: HeatGuard mapping (configurable). Categories are defined by which documented work/rest regime keeps the 1-hour exposure within the applicable NIOSH limit, not by fixed WBGT values.

categories.label: Routine monitoring
categories.rule: Effective WBGT below the applicable limit at the crew's current work/rest regime by at least the caution margin.

categories.label: Caution
categories.rule: Effective WBGT within the caution margin of the applicable limit at the current regime.

categories.label: Elevated
categories.rule: Applicable limit exceeded at the current regime; a 45/15 work/rest regime would bring the TWA within the limit.

categories.label: High
categories.rule: Applicable limit exceeded; only a 30/30 or 15/45 work/rest regime would bring the TWA within the limit.

categories.label: Critical
categories.rule: Applicable limit exceeded even with a 15/45 work/rest regime.

site_policy.caution_margin_source: Site policy setting (configurable). NOT a NIOSH value: it only controls how early an 'approaching the limit' caution is raised.
site_policy.averaging_note: NIOSH limits are 1-hour TWAs. HeatGuard screens with max(latest effective WBGT, rolling 60-simulated-minute mean) so that improving conditions do not instantly clear a concern and rising conditions are recognised without waiting an hour.

hydration: NIOSH 2016 recommends that workers in the heat drink about 1 cup (8 oz, ~237 mL) of water every 15-20 minutes during moderate activity in moderately hot conditions; for prolonged sweating lasting several hours, sports drinks containing balanced electrolytes may be considered.
limitations: RAL/REL apply to healthy workers; individual susceptibility (medical conditions, medications, prior heat illness) is not assessed.
Limits are 1-hour TWAs; short-interval readings are screened conservatively, not averaged exactly as specified.
Metabolic rates are category estimates, not measurements.
WBGT-based limits are not valid for encapsulating or vapour-barrier ensembles without expert review.
This is decision support only; it does not diagnose heat illness or clear any worker to resume work.
